title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S → T is a morphism of schemes. E is an O_S-module with a stratification δ = δ^∞_E relative to T, i.e. an isomorphism p_1^*E ≅ p_2^*E on the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal, presented as a map E → P^∞_{S/T}(E). P is an affine torsor under E: a sheaf of sets with a simply transitive E-action, x ↦ x+ξ. Up to isomorphism such torsors are classes in H^1(S,E), i.e. extensions of O_S by E.

Previous page. Grothendieck identifies three things.
- A stratification on P compatible with δ is the same as a map (26) λ: P → P^∞_{S/T}(E)/δE satisfying conditions (27) and (28).
- Via the additive splitting (29), P^∞(E)^+ ≅ P^∞(E)/δE, where P^∞(E)^+ is the 'augmentation kernel' of jets. This gives the map λ^+: P → P^∞(E)^+ of (30).
- λ^+ satisfies the twisted additivity (31): λ^+(x+ξ) = λ^+(x) + d^+(ξ), with d^+(ξ) = d^∞(ξ) − δ^∞(ξ).

This page, first part.
- Truncating at order 1 uses P^1_{S/T}(E)^+ = E⊗Ω^1_{S/T}. This gives (32) d^0_P: P → E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} with d^0_P(x+ξ) = d^0_P(x) + d^0_E(ξ), where d^0_E is the connection on E coming from δ (via (23)).
- So d^0_P is an affine connection on the torsor P lifting the connection of E.
- Grothendieck states three facts, with the marginal note 'faire la vérification':
  - this is exactly the connection that the stratification of P induces;
  - it is integrable;
  - its class in H^1_DR(S,E) is the image, under the canonical comparison map (24) H^1_Strat(S,E) → H^1_DR(S,E), of the class of (P,λ).
- In modern terms: a torsor with compatible connection ↔ an extension 0 → E → Ẽ → O_S → 0 in the category of modules with integrable connection. The page proves that the 'stratified ↦ de Rham' map on such extension classes agrees with the comparison map in degree 1.

This page, Corollary. Assume T has characteristic 0 and Ω^1_{S/T} is flat (e.g. S formally smooth over T), so that (24) is an isomorphism. Then:
- stratifications of P compatible with that of E ↔ integrable connections on P compatible with that of E;
- hence also ↔ maps λ (or λ^+) satisfying (27), (28), (31);
- hence also ↔ homomorphisms d_P as in (17)/(18), by reduction to first order (completed on the next page).

The marginal NB recalls the linear analogue: stratifications on E ↔ integrable connections on E.

Next page.
- Taking P = E (the trivial torsor) shows that reduction gives an isomorphism of sheaves between horizontal sections of P^∞(E)^+ and closed 1-forms Z^1(E⊗Ω^1). That is, a closed E-valued 1-form integrates canonically to an ∞-jet. This is a sheaf-level Poincaré-lemma statement for the first stratified/de Rham cohomology.
- §4 then starts Picard–Fuchs equations, using an exact sequence 0 → E' → E → E'' → 0 with E' not horizontal.
- The purpose of §3 is to make the torsor/extension language for H^1 available for that construction.
errors: The formula '(32) ... d^b_E(x) = λ^+(x) mod ...' is a slip. It should read d^0_P(x) = λ^+(x) mod (terms of order ≥2), i.e. d_P is the order-1 truncation of λ^+.
'P un torseur sur E' should be 'torseur sous E' (P is a torsor under E).
The verification that the truncated map is the induced connection, is integrable, and has the right cohomology class is explicitly left undone ('faire la vérification'). Each step is routine.

The hypothesis 'Ω^1_{S/T} plat' alone is weaker than what the standard equivalence (stratification ↔ integrable connection, comparison (24) bijective) requires. One really needs formal smoothness, or at least local freeness of the P^n_{S/T}. The parenthetical 'p.ex. S formellement lisse' is the safe hypothesis. Grothendieck refers back to (24) for the exact conditions, so this is at most an imprecise gloss.

ideas.what: Affine torsors under a stratified (resp. flat-connection) module, with compatible stratification (resp. connection), and their classification by H^1_Strat(S,E) (resp. H^1_DR(S,E))
ideas.modern_name: Ext^1(O_S, E) in the category of crystals / D-modules = H^1_crys / H^1_DR; extensions of flat bundles
ideas.where_published: Spirit close to 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); the torsor formulation in particular is unsure

ideas.what: Order-1 truncation of the jet-valued map λ^+ gives an affine connection d_P with d_P(x+ξ) = d_P(x) + ∇ξ, compatible with the comparison map H^1_Strat → H^1_DR
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the stratification↔connection dictionary with degree-1 comparison of crystalline/de Rham cohomology

ideas.what: In characteristic 0 for S formally smooth, compatible stratifications on a torsor ↔ compatible integrable connections; and horizontal elements of P^∞(E)^+ ↔ closed E-valued 1-forms
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of stratifications and integrable connections in char 0 (affine/torsor version); formal Poincaré lemma in degree 1
ideas.where_published: Linear case in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine torsor version of the classical stratification/integrable-connection equivalence in characteristic 0, plus the degree-1 comparison of stratified and de Rham cohomology. All of this is standard since Grothendieck's 1966 crystals lectures and Berthelot/Katz–Oda. The only unpublished flavour is the explicit jet-level formulas (29)–(32), which serve as preparation for a torsor-style derivation of Picard–Fuchs equations on the following pages.
transcription_corrections: 'd^*_P' in (32) and in the formula below it is most likely d^0_P (the order-0 differential / connection map), matching the notation of the previous page; likewise 'd^*_E(ξ)' should be d^0_E(ξ).
'd^b_E(x) = λ^+(x) mod ...' should read 'd^0_P(x) = λ^+(x) mod ...'.
'P un torseur sur E' reads in context as 'P un torseur sous E'.
In the corollary, the bracket reads '[i.e. aussi, λ^+ : P → P^∞_{S/T}(E)^+]', with the final '+' attached to the bracketed jet sheaf; the struck item before '(31)' is illegible.
The bottom right addition reads 'et à valeurs dans P^∞_{S/T}(E)^+' (continuation of the condition list).
